scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): agrees that welfare is the surest indicator while arguing achievements still matter; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Nations are often remembered for their famous leaders, artists, and scientists.
One claim holds that the surest indicator of a great nation is not these achievements, on the reason that it is really the welfare of all its people.
I largely agree that welfare is the truest measure, but I believe great achievements still matter as part of it.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why welfare is the surest indicator

sentences.text: First, the reason behind the claim is sound, because the welfare of the people is the clearest test of greatness.
A nation may boast brilliant achievements while most of its citizens remain poor and powerless.
For example, a country with famous monuments but starving people has failed at its most basic duty.
This shows that achievements mean little if the ordinary people do not live decent lives.
Widespread health, safety, and opportunity touch everyone, not just a gifted few.
Any nation that cares for all its people has fulfilled its deepest purpose.
To this extent, the reason rightly points to welfare as the surest indicator.
Second, however, the claim goes too far in dismissing achievements entirely.
Great discoveries and works of art often improve the welfare of the people themselves.
Consider how medical research lengthens ordinary lives or how great art enriches a whole culture.
Such achievements are often a cause of welfare rather than something separate from it.
Countries that value learning and creativity tend to grow healthier and wealthier as well.
Achievements can also give a people pride and a shared sense of who they are.
Welfare and achievement, then, support each other rather than standing apart.
In conclusion, I agree that the welfare of the people is the truest measure of a great nation.
But great achievements should not be dismissed, since they often raise that very welfare.
Greatness belongs to the nation that turns its achievements toward the good of all its people.
